newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end weaker, gold rangebound.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end weaker, gold rangebound.

text.p: New York precious metals ended weaker Thursday, with little activity in the rangebound gold and silver markets, while platinum and palladium ended sharply weaker as the market digested this week's news from Russia of an imminent resumption in white metal exports, dealers said.
Floor sources said dealings in COMEX gold were muted and largely confined to rolling over positions from the June to August contracts.
COMEX June gold settled $0.50 weaker at $343.20 an ounce, traded $343.90 to $342.70.
Late afternoon bullion was quoted at $342.40/90.
COMEX July silver settled 1.7 cents weaker at $4.678, traded $4.69 to $4.66.
Estimated volume in gold and silver were 43,000 and 7,000, respectively.
June NYMEX palladium ended down $4.75 at $175.35, traded $177.00 to $174.50. July NYMEX platinum finished $3.10 lower at $389.00, traded $391.50 to $386.50.
The weaker closes in the white metals belied the high lease rates in palladium, and the 2.0 to 3.0 percent surge in platinum lease rates Thursday, dealers said.
NYMEX metals and its COMEX division futures will close early on Friday at 1300 EDT for palladium and copper, 1305 for silver, and 1310 for platinum and gold.
NYMEX and COMEX are shut Memorial Day Monday.
